utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-14/2-T, the Prosecutor versus Dario Kordic and Mario Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Sayers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Cicak.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Good morning. How are you today?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Fine, thank you. We were just going through the chronological documents that you had been shown by the Prosecution during your examination in chief, and we had just finished going through the document that was marked D7, or Z7, minutes of the meeting of the HDZ, Travnik region, on July the 21st, 1991. I think that I finished going over the questions that I had for you at that document, and I thank you for your answers.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I just (inaudible).

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: The next document, Mr. Cicak, that you were shown by the Prosecution chronologically was a document that was marked Z8, dated July 30th, 1991, and I wonder if the usher would just put that in front of you. You have the document, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. And as I understand it, it was Mr. Anto Valenta that called this meeting for July the 30th, 1999. Did you know anything about that meeting before it was called by Mr. Valenta?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I knew that a meeting was being prepared, but you forget one thing: This meeting was called on the 30th of July, 1991, at 20.00 hours, and that meant that I could not attend the meeting at that time because I am rather far away from the place of venue of such meeting, so that all the meetings that took place at 8.00 or 9.00 or 10.00 in the evening, I simply could not attend them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. So you were not present at this meeting, I take it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. You can see that Mr. Kordic is listed as one of the many attendees at this meeting, and he's listed on page 1; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. All the presidents of all municipal boards of the HDZ in the region, in the Lasva region, were invited to the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. And one of the agenda items to be discussed was a public HDZ panel to be convened in the town of Vitez on August the 4th, 1991, just a few days later. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: If you take a look at page 2 of this document, item number 2, the recommendation was that the panel be regional in character and that Croatians as well as Muslim people would be invited to take part in it. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Did you attend that panel discussion when it was ultimately convened?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I believe I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. One of the main themes of discussion was the question of whether recruits should continue to be sent to the JNA army. Do you remember discussing that particular subject?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I remember it. It was general agreement not only by political parties but also of the citizens of Bosnia-Herzegovina, was that young men from Bosnia-Herzegovina, regardless of their ethnic origin, should not be sent to the regular troops as recruits to the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: There was vigorous opposition, both amongst the Croatian Community and the Muslim community in the Travnik region, to the proposition that recruits should continue to be sent to an army that was actively waging a war of aggression against neighbouring republics; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, there was fierce opposition. I believe that young men followed the advice and did not accept to be recruited.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say, Mr. Cicak, that you were an advocate of that particular recommendation, that young men in the area should refrain from volunteering their services to the JNA?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was not directly involved in this business, because I had other duties in the municipal organisation of the HDZ, but I would have done the same as others. That is, I would have resisted and not allowed young men from Bosnia-Herzegovina to participate in any aggressive action against neighbouring republics.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Even if the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina actually recommended the conscription of recruits into the JNA; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think that the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina would never take such a decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Now, item number 3 of the discussion items here is that support should be given to an HDZ initiative to set up a new Croatian government which would consist of Croatian experts regardless of their political orientation. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: But that reference is to the new government that was to be set up in Croatia after the declaration of independence by Croatia in June of 1991, following the referendum a month earlier; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I am quite sure that it refers to the government of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: That's the point I was making. I think that we can now pass on to the provision of item 3 that says: "Because of its geographic position and because it is a centre of the district, municipal HDZ board in Busovaca is appointed headquarters of the Travnik regional community." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And indeed, sir, after this particular meeting, further meetings of the Travnik regional community were actually held in Busovaca, the town of Busovaca; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Now, if you take a look at the final portion of these minutes, sir, a recommendation was made by the Travnik regional community to both the presidency of the HDZ in Bosnia and Herzegovina and also to the regional War Council to start working on a proposal of plans to protect the entire population -- or "the population," it says -- from the danger of war that could erupt at any moment. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: That was a position that you agreed with too? I mean, it was being actively discussed amongst the political leadership in the HDZ at that time, wasn't it, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I did, except that I requested that from the president of the presidency, all active ministers, deputy ministers, and other people, take an active part in the protection of Bosnia-Herzegovina against military operations. Unfortunately, I failed. And then this is not the duty of the HDZ, as a party.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Well, the comment that is made right at the end of the minutes is prescient, is it not, Mr. Cicak, because just a few days later, there was a massive Serbian military attack on the city of Vukovar in eastern Croatia; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And just so that we can set the historical context for Their Honours' understanding, as of this time, Croatia was still not an independent country, was it? Do you recall my --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter says, "Sorry, we could not hear the answer."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Sorry, I spoke over you, sir. My question was, "As of the time of these minutes, Croatia was still not an independent country?" I think you said you agreed with that.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Just a moment. Croatia had a somewhat longer period during which it was -- its independence was recognised, so I do not know which date you have in mind. There is the 25th of June, when it proclaimed its independence. Then it was postponed until the 8th of October, '91. Then on the 15th of January, '92, it was recognised by the European Union and only after that by the United Nations, so it was quite a long period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Right, that's the point I was making, and I think you agree with me. The first step towards the realisation of independence for the Republic of Croatia was its declaration of independence on June the 25th, I believe, of 1991; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, the 25th of June, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Pursuant to an agreement reached at the town of Brioni, I believe, sir, that the Croatian authorities agreed to delay the carrying into effect of that declaration of independence until October the 8th of 1991; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Until the 8th of October, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Precisely. And as of that time, it was still uncertain whether the international community would actually recognise Croatia as an independent country? There was some uncertainty in that regard; don't you agree?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I agree, and I could not understand why the international community was procrastinating with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Right, sir. But whatever the reason for that procrastination, I believe the first country to recognise the independence of Croatia was actually Germany on Christmas Eve of 1992. Is that consistent with your recollection?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Then the international community actually recognised the independence of Croatia following upon the German recognition on January the 15th of 1992, which was one day before the speech that you talked about in your direct examination in Busovaca; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: At that meeting, I did not take the floor, but I did say something during a discussion with the officials of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I agree with that. But the point I was making was that that speech occurred just one day after the recognition of Croatia as an independent country by the international community at large.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Now, to get back to these minutes, Exhibit Z8, as of their date, July the 30th, 1991, Bosnia-Herzegovina was still one of the constituent republics left in what used to be the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: You mean the rest of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: That's exactly right, and you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: This is, just to set the general stage here, this is certainly a time of turmoil and confusion, politically and militarily, in the former Yugoslavia, is it not, sir? You lived through it. You can certainly tell us that.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, with pleasure, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Well, I'll tell you what, let's go over to the next exhibit that the Prosecutor showed you, Exhibit Z9, which is a copy of the minutes of the HDZ of the Travnik region of August the 13th, 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I have Z11.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Is it Z11? I'm sorry. My apologies to the Trial Chamber for misidentifying the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You have Exhibit Z11 in front of you, Mr. Cicak?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know what these markings are, but could you give me the date and what it is about?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. It says, "August the 13th, 1991," and it appears to be a copy of the minutes of a meeting of the HDZ for the Travnik region on that date. Do you remember testifying about this particular document, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You were one of the seven attendees at this meeting from the Busovaca opstina; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: This session was actually held in Busovaca, was it not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: It was attended by Mr. Mate Boban, as one of the guests --

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, he was present. Yes, Mr. Mate Boban was present, Professor Martin Udovicic and Dr. Vjekoslav Barac. They were not guests there, they were part of the HDZ B and H, and it was only natural for them to attend that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Now, on the subject of Mr. Martin Udovicic, there isn't any doubt he was present at this meeting in Busovaca; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: (No audible response)

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: So he didn't object to having the Travnik regional community meetings moved from Travnik to Busovaca, did he, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have my particular opinion on that. If you're interested, I can tell you. If not, then I won't say anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Well, you said, at page 1194 of your first day of testimony, that it would be inconceivable that a former president who headed the regional community of Travnik, that is, Professor Martin Udovicic, should leave the leadership of the regional community and its movement to Busovaca. Do you remember that testimony?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Nonetheless, here is Mr. Udovicic in Busovaca for a meeting of the Travnik regional community on August 13th of 1991, and you were there; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Now, the first item on the agenda, Mr. Cicak, was an analysis of the decisions reached by the main board of the HDZ BiH on --

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: May I add a word to your former question, because I did not complete my answer? If I may, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. Martin Udovicic and Mr. Vjekoslav Barac were impotent -- were quite helpless in the Travnik region as against Mr. Kordic and his mentor, Mate Boban, because Mr. Mate Boban, together with Kordic, was asking that the regional community be transferred to Busovaca. So that Mr. Martin Udovicic, who is a very noble man, a professor and educated, Dr. Vjekoslav Barac, who is a physician, another noble man, were simply helpless before that, and they could not stop something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, isn't it true that it was at this meeting, this was the only time that you ever actually met Mate Boban in the town of Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. I met Mr. Mate Boban several times, but we were never on good terms. So when we met in Busovaca for the first time, we dissented right away, that is, as far as the interpretation of the democracy. I saw it one way and he saw it the other way. He embraced a very national -- rather nationalistic perception of Croats, and I embraced a democratic solution to problems with all the ethnicities living in Bosnia-Herzegovina. And that conflict lasted until his departure; that is, our misunderstandings.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Let me focus you back on the question I asked you, sir, if you could just for a minute. Isn't it true that you only ever met Mr. Mate Boban once in the town of Busovaca? You may have had meetings with him in other places, but you only met him once in Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, several times in Busovaca, not once only, and that was not the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Now, the first item on the agenda, as I tried to ask you earlier, was an analysis of the decisions of the main board of the HDZ BiH reached on August the 6th of 1991? You see that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: You mean item 1, "Conclusions"?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: No, item 1 of the agenda.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Sorry. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You weren't actually present at the meeting at the main board held on that date, were you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I was not, but I spoke to the members of the main board about those conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Did you ever see a copy of the minutes of that particular meeting, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think that nobody in the HDZ ever saw original minutes of any meeting at all. They always received minutes made by Mr. Kostroman.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Did you ever see a copy of the minutes of the August the 6th, 1991 meeting, sir, of the main board of the HDZ BiH?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have to think about which meeting it was, and I can't really know offhand which meeting it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Do you mean that?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: How do you mean? Well, let's move on. Busovaca is actually one of 14 separate municipalities that was represented by elected representatives at this meeting; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Busovaca was represented by a representative or rather since it happened in Busovaca, there were several members of the municipal board. Normally, there is one representative attending such meetings on behalf -- at the regional community.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Right, but there were 14 separate municipalities represented here. That's the simple question that I'm asking. That's pretty obvious, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: If you take a look at the decision, sir, just a few that I would like to discuss with you that I don't believe were covered by the Prosecutor when they covered this document with you, item number 2 states that the decisions of the Travnik regional community are supported by all municipality boards of the HDZ BiH. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: That includes the decision to move the Travnik regional community headquarters to Busovaca; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Now let's turn to paragraph 3. I'm not sure I understood your testimony during direct examination. This paragraph states that the behaviour of Stjepan Kljujic, the president of the HDZ BiH, while he conducted the session of the HDZ BiH main board on 6 August, 1991, is judged as unbefitting and unacceptable.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: An excellent question. Both questions are very excellent. Namely, if you look at it a little bit, if you're an analyst and if you engage in politics, you will see that these meetings, which are of vital importance for Bosnia-Herzegovina, Mr. Stjepan Kljujic has not been invited to them. That is, the president of the party, the president of the party is not invited to a meeting which is of utmost importance for Bosnia-Herzegovina, and secondly, the general secretary, Mr. Markesic, is not invited to that meeting either. The meeting is conducted by an ordinary administrative clerk, Ignac Kostroman, so that all this, if you look at it in the light of all the other developments, means that the 13th of August, 1991, was the beginning of dismissal of Mr. Kljujic from the post of presidency and the move, the transfer, the shift of the presidency of the HDZ to Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Mr. Kljujic was a pretty popular character, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, he was quite popular. He remained popular, and he's still popular.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: In fact, he didn't like working very hard, did he, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is his own personal affair.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Well, that was your personal opinion, too, wasn't it? That's what you told the Prosecutors four or five months ago.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Since we are good friends, I don't know. I didn't realise that the Prosecutor would be registering every little word I said. We are close personal friends. I know how he behaves and he knows how I behave, so from now on I'm going to watch what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You did tell the Prosecutors just four or five months ago, on page 3 of your statement, that even though he was a media personality and charming, he worked very little; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Sayers, I think the witness has answered that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I fully concur, Your Honour, and I'll move on swiftly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Turning to the subparagraph (a) of main paragraph 4 of this document, sir, a proposal was made at this meeting that you attended, the HDZ BiH secretariat should "solicit resumes from distinguished Croat intellectuals in order to establish proper records on potential cadres." You certainly agreed with that proposition, did you not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I absolutely disagreed. This is a continuation of the communist practice of registering persons who are positive and others who are not positive, those who are good and those who are bad. However, this point 4 is a continuation of points 2 and 3 that I talked about, that is to say, a complete separation of the centre of the HVO, Mr. Kljujic and Mr. Markesic, and again, making new files and being annexed to Herceg-Bosna, that is to say Mate Boban and Dario Kordic, who would go on leading the HVO and the southern part. But Posavina, the northern part, was much smarter, and they didn't allow others to interfere in their own affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Well, let's turn to paragraph 7 of this document. The regional community boards were instructed, and other boards were encouraged, "to make contact with Mate Boban to familiarise themselves with the superior level of organisation in certain Herzegovinian municipality boards and to exchange useful information in the new situation." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Very good. Very good. You put your questions very well. This is a continuation of points 2, 3, and 4. Now we have point 7. So this is an obvious example of the fact that everything had to be concentrated on Mr. Mate Boban. This is a telling example of how this was done. Everything was supposed to be oriented towards Mr. Mate Boban. You put your questions remarkably well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Thank you. And actually, Mr. Udovicic was the gentleman that suggested this, and that vote was -- a vote was taken on that suggestion, and it was approved at the meeting that you attended; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. After that, Mr. Udovicic moved away with his entire family. He went to Zagreb, and that is where he lives until the present day, and I think that he stopped all HDZ activities, and most probably he doesn't even want to remember having belonged to the HDZ, ever.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: So after August the 13th, 1991, Mr. Udovicic was off to Zagreb and didn't attend any further meetings of the party political organisation in the Travnik region?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Please, don't take my word for every date that is mentioned. I don't know whether he left on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, or Friday. I don't know whether he left at 3.00, 4.00, or 5.00. Please don't insist on these minute details.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Let's turn our attention to paragraph 11 of the document, where the declaration is made that "It is indispensable to activate our Security Council immediately because there can be no delay. Any delay will cause unforeseeable consequences for the Croatian people. " That was one of the proposals that was discussed and agreed upon at this meeting that you attended; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Indeed, if you take a look at paragraph 13, a recommendation is made by the Travnik regional community that the presidency should take a clear stand on the participation of Croatian clubs in sports events because of recent Greater Serbian propaganda in that milieu. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You agreed with that, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Absolutely. The point was that there were matches that were played between the national teams of Bosnia-Herzegovina and Serbia, and there were certain incidents, and we don't want to spread this to the other state, but this did take place in the other state too. So I think that this is in the context of the right kind of policy that should be pursued, a democratic policy, and that is to say to avoid incidents that certain persons are prone to.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And indeed, that's the essence of democracy, isn't it? Making recommendations, having the right to make recommendations which may or may not be accepted according to the will of the majority?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't understand what you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Nor do I. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Coming to the next exhibit --

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: If you don't understand him, what's left for me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Now, don't comment, please, Mr. Cicak, and we'll move more quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Moving to the next exhibit --

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I wish we would move faster.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We will move faster, if, Mr. Cicak, you do not comment on the evidence. Could you remember, please, that you are here to give evidence, not to comment. Counsel is here asking you questions, that's his job, and if you don't comment, we will move more quickly. Yes, Mr. Sayers. Can we move on? We've only dealt with two documents in three-quarters of an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I'm very sorry for that, Your Honour, and I'll try to move much more quickly. Turning to Exhibit Z12, which is the minutes of a meeting dated August 23rd, 1991 -- and if I may, just for the Court's easy reference, I've prepared a graphic organisational chart of the way that the HDZ looked, with all of its municipalities, as of the date of this particular document. All right, Mr. Cicak, trying to move right along here, this was a meeting of the -- this represents conclusions reached by the presidency of the HDZ BiH dated August the 23rd, 1991. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know. This paper was sent by Mr. Kostroman. He was not authorised to do that. But let's accept it as such.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: It reflects the division, organisational division of the party in Bosnia-Herzegovina into nine separate regions, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Those nine separate regions covered 70 separate municipalities; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Busovaca was just one of those 70 municipalities; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You were just one of three vice-presidents of that municipality at this time, August of 1991; that's fair to say, is it not? Is that fair to say, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: At first glance one could say so. However, I was equally important not only as the vice-president but also as a prominent citizen in all the municipalities of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I mentioned earlier on that there were 110 municipalities in Bosnia-Herzegovina. You say there were 70-something municipalities, but Croats lived in all 110 municipalities of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and I took care of them. I was concerned about their safety, security, their work, their well-being.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now let's turn to the next exhibit, if I may, Exhibit Z13.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Before we do that, we need a number for this structure. What is the number, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The number is D11/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Judge Bennouna's microphone isn't working -- is now working.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Mr. Sayers, the witness has just told us that he was not only the vice-president of the regional community of Travnik, but that he was also an eminent personality charged with intervening and protecting Croats, the Croats in all the other municipalities. I think we were told that there were a lot of municipalities there. Could we know, on the basis of what Mr. Cicak was authorised to protect eminent personalities, those 110 people, I mean, he was the vice-president of the Travnik community as we see here but under what authority did he act in that respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I think that is a very excellent question, Judge Bennouna, and I just open the floor up to Mr. Cicak to answer by what authority he purported to represent the Croatian people at this time.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: At that time, no authority was needed. I did not represent the Croat people. I was talking about the reputation I enjoyed among the Croat people and not only among the Croat people but also among the Muslim and the Serb peoples. That is to say, that I communicated in all these municipalities, and it was not attached to a special mandate or office, but citizens from various municipalities wherever I appeared received me as if I were one of their own. They talked to me, they talked about the problems that were the most topical at that point and I could move from one part of Bosnia-Herzegovina to another part of Bosnia-Herzegovina, talk to citizens of all ethnic backgrounds without any danger, without any mandate, without any recommendations, and I could present those conclusions at any meeting of the Croatian Democratic Union or other associations wherever I might have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And, Judge Bennouna, there was one premise to your question which I think was not factually correct although it's easy to be confused. It took me a long time to figure this out, but I do not believe that Mr. Cicak was the vice-president of the Travnik regional community at any time, and I'd just like to ask him a question in that regard, if I may.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Mr. Cicak, it's true, isn't it, that you were actually one of the three vice-presidents of the very lowest level of party organisation, the Busovaca municipality, and that you never actually enjoyed any formal office at the regional community level?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think that you're operating with the wrong information. Apart from the office I held in Busovaca, I was a member of the court of honour, and the disciplinary court of the main board of the HDZ of Bosnia-Herzegovina, so Busovaca was not really my point of departure. I personally had a far broader range, scope, than merely Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) There it is. Yes. Right. I wanted to say, according to the table that we have, the vice-president of the municipality -- in the municipality of Busovaca, that is what we have in the document here. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Thank you very much indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Mr. Cicak, were you elected or appointed to the positions in the HDZ that you've just described, other than the position of vice-president of the local party board at the Busovaca level?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was elected at the convention.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Now, turning to Exhibit Z13, which I believe is the next exhibit chronologically, I only have two questions, and believe me, sir, they are both extremely short. First, do you see the provision of this document that says that the state of emergency requires round the clock duties and alertness in the municipal HDZ BiH boards, including the monitoring of military formations in the field?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Do you also see the instruction that the municipal boards were to contact their counterparts at the SDA to come up with joint defence preparations?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. We can now go on to the next exhibit, Z14, if I may. The date of this document is August the 29th of 1991. Did you know anything about the peace conferences under way two days earlier? I believe that was the Badinter EC Arbitration Commission. Did you know anything about that, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know, but I wasn't really interested in that, because I knew that those conferences were bound to fail.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Now, you were actually at this particular meeting held in Busovaca at the lowest level of the party organisation, the municipal level, on August the 29th, 1991; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know what meeting you're referring to. Oh, yes, the 29th. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You were one of the authors of this particular document, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Possibly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. And at this time, of course, Mr. Cicak, it's well known to all people in Bosnia-Herzegovina that Vukovar had been attacked and was besieged by this time; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Article 3 of this document provides that the executive board of the municipal organisation would become the command of the municipal HDZ BiH organisation in exceptional or wartime conditions. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Going on to the next article, sir, the decision made on August the 29th, 1991, was that the president of the municipal HDZ organisation in Busovaca would become the commander, with his assistants, the deputy president, secretaries and treasurer, and they would have the same post in the command. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You didn't know that Mr. Kordic ceased to be president of the municipal organisation on April the 1st of 1992, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Sorry, the witness's answer was inaudible to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Would you repeat your answer, Mr. Cicak, because the interpreter didn't get it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it's clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Just three short questions to conclude this document, or four, if I may. The Security Council was to be made up of eight members, is that correct, according to Article 6? You do agree with that, don't you? I mean it says it in pretty clear language.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. Sorry. If I pause, it doesn't mean I don't agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: No problem. Then in Article 9, of course, it says that the Security Council, the eight members of the Security Council, all have to act jointly with respect to decisions that they make. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. The Prosecutor asked you some questions in connection with Article 14, I believe, of this document, regarding release of information to the press, and there was some implication made in that connection, and I would just like to ask you to agree with me that it's a pretty good idea, in wartime conditions, to restrict access of information about your resources, people, organisation, to the enemy. That's a fairly general proposition that you would accept; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, a standard one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. That completes the questions I have for this document. Let's move on to the next one, if I might. Exhibit Z16.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Can I put a question? Can I put another question in relation to this? I mean an answer. I want to give an answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Which document is it you want to give an answer about? The last one, the one that we've just dealt with? Yes, if you could, briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: The Defence did not let me do so. I'll be very brief. First of all, this is a very good document that Mr. Kordic never abided by. Here there is an obligation to let the municipal organisation know about certain things and to have them give their consent in terms of what the HDZ is doing, including the HDZ Busovaca. Mr. Kordic never abided by this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cicak. We've heard your views on that regard before. And with that in mind, let's turn to the activity of the party at the national level, and that's Exhibit Z16. These are the minutes of a meeting of the Security Council of the HDZ BiH at the national level, held on September the 18th, 1991, and they are actually signed by Stjepan Kljujic; isn't that right, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: How do you mean you're not sure?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't see why he would sign the same document twice. Why would you put one signature by the other? I mean a person would really have to be very tipsy or have something happen to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Well, let's take a look at the signature page. You recognise the signature of the person that you've described as your good friend, don't you, Mr. Kljujic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: He signs this in what capacity, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: It says here that he signs in the capacity of president.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Right. And the signature to the left of his is the signature of Ignac Kostroman, I believe. Right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: In what capacity, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: The administrative secretary.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Now, let's go through this document --

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: You didn't give me an answer. Why is there another signature of Mr. Kljujic's here? Okay, you don't even have to answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: This was a meeting held in the town of Konjic. Is that right, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did not attend that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You were not there. All right.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Item 1 of the conclusions reached by the Security Council on that day is that the Security Council is renamed the Crisis Staff; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And the Crisis Staff actually consists, as I count them, of 13 members.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Their names are listed in a separate attachment to this document; right, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Now, this document that Mr. Kljujic signed directed the political executive crisis staff, or directed the staff, rather, to form a professional command organ which would be a professional military body. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: (Inaudible response)

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Mr. Kljujic issues an order to begin immediately to direct the entire HDZ and the Croatian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina to arrange for the procurement of weapons. The document says that in black and white, does it not, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: The president of the Crisis Staff is not Mr. Boban at all, it's Mr. Kljujic, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is Kljujic's last -- or rather I think that Kljujic spoke only on one more occasion, and then he no longer appeared in HDZ politics.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: But as of the 18th of September, 1991, when he issued this directive, he was the president of the Crisis Staff, wasn't he, sir? You're not disagreeing with that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Just a small correction. On that day, a meeting of the presidency was held, and it was renamed into the Crisis Staff. That is to say that a meeting of the presidency of the HDZ of BH was held, and a decision was reached straightaway that it would no longer be called the presidency of the BH HDZ but it would be called the Crisis Staff, as we've just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. And you see, at the bottom of the page, the directive issued by the Crisis Staff that reads as follows: "In the event of armed conflict on territories with predominantly Croatian populations, the Crisis Staff shall assume all powers in the municipalities, and the work of the BH HDZ shall temporarily cease until the threat of war has passed; i.e., until the Crisis Staff makes such an assessment."

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Do you remember any discussion of that directive issued by President Kljujic of this organisation at the local level in Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I responded quite vehemently to this -- quite sharply to this decision, because I knew what it would end up in; that is, the formation of ethnically-pure environments and that where there was a majority population somewhere, then a particular group should take over the power. That is, where the Serbs were the majority, Serbs should take over the power. Where Croats were the majority of the population in a particular area, Croats should take power, and where the Muslims were the majority, Muslims should take power. It is completely opposite to any democratic ideas at all. And in case of war, all these matters should have been resolved in a completely different manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: So it's fair to say that you vehemently and vociferously disagreed with the decision signed by the person you that described as your good friend?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That's a matter of comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I'll move on, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Turning to paragraph 5 of this document --

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: It has nothing to do -- friendship and politics are two different things.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: This paragraph reads: "Stjepan Kljujic is required immediately to contact the leadership of the SDA/Party of Democratic Action/and to seek a political declaration from them. But the Crisis Staff shall develop plans of action both with and without the SDA and shall undertake concrete measures for this purpose." Was there any discussion of that in Busovaca when you met with the elected party representatives at the local level, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: This was something that Mr. Kljujic was charged with, but the municipal board or the Croatian Democratic Community in Busovaca on a number of occasions spoke to the SDA leadership, recommending them to prepare people for the misfortune looming over Bosnia-Herzegovina. However, they responded -- they replied that they were not ready at the time, and I believe it simply turned out like that. They simply thought that somebody else would solve it, solve the question. But nobody else could solve that question but the people of Bosnia and Herzegovina. That is, jointly Muslims, Bosniaks, were not interested, at first, in defending themselves; that is, they were not ready for that critical point in time. And that is why it was decided to recommend to continue negotiations with them. I do not know whether this met with any success or not. When I was there, it did not prove successful.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Three other short questions on this document. Would you turn to paragraph 8, please? It would be fair to say that this is, at the highest level of the party, nationally, a continuation of the discussion that we've seen in the earlier documents, and the conclusion at the national party level was that municipalities should not send recruits to the JNA and that no mobilisations would be permitted except mobilisations carried out through the crisis staffs of the party?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. This recommendation is well worded here, but it doesn't refer to the Croatian Democratic Union only but to the State of Bosnia-Herzegovina at large, from the president of the presidency down to the last citizen. It was decided that recruits should not be sent to serve their military duty with the Yugoslav People's Army, that is, not to be sent outside the frontiers of Bosnia-Herzegovina and not to be sent to serve, again, their military service with the Yugoslav People's Army. Subsequently, it resulted in a series of very unpleasant scenes across Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Now, at this time in the middle of September of 1991, the future of Bosnia-Herzegovina, as a country, was up in the air, it was uncertain. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Indeed, there were numerous proposals being discussed amongst all of the political parties in the country as to what the country would look like a year or two from that particular point in time. Would that be fair to say?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Was one of those proposals that was being discussed nationally and by the HDZ, both at the local and the national level, a proposal for some kind of canonisation of the various regions in the country?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And that canonisation would proceed along, I believe, pretty much ethnic lines; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Indeed the document signed by Stjepan Kljujic calls for the appointment of a commission for canonisation in paragraph 11 of this document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Indeed it also calls for the appointment of certain members to that commission. I wonder if you would just take a look at the people who were appointed to that commission, sir. They are all pretty respectable, well-credentialed, intellectual people, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: What page is it? Will you tell me?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: It's paragraph 11 of the document, page 3.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: They include, of course, Dr. Milenko Brkic from Mostar; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Mariofil Ljubic is here, Mr. Pandzic, Mr. Markesic, Miro Lasic, Milenko Brkic, Vlatko Kraljevic, Ivan Komsic and Zoran Perkovic. At that time, some of them are prominent citizens -- rather politicians of Bosnia-Herzegovina to this day.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: The final point I want to make about this document appears just after --

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have not finished with this. If I may, Your Honours, may I add just one word?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. Kljujic was planning to perform the canonisation of Bosnia-Herzegovina with mixed population, that is, that every canton would have Muslims, Croats, Serbs. The other side, headed by Mr. Boban, Mr. Kordic, Mr. Tudjman and all the others, wanted the canonisation to follow purely ethnical principles; that is, to have a Croat canton, a Serb canton, and a Muslim or Bosniak canton. I opposed that idea, but I was alone in that, just as I am alone today when, again, there is talk about the ethnic division of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right, sir. Now, if you could just turn to page 3 of the document, this document was to be kept strictly confidential, wasn't it? I'm sorry, it's on page 4 of the Croatian version.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Please go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You would agree that this document was to be kept strictly confidential?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Now, just stepping back a little bit to place this document in the historical context, were you aware that the peace conference had been convened right here, actually, in The Hague on September the 7th of 1991, and that it was actually chaired by Lord Carrington?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Go on, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Were you aware that the Serbian autonomous region of Eastern Herzegovina was declared six days before this document, sir, on September the 12th, 1991?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And that's something, I take it, sir, that caused you the utmost of concern.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: The whole procedure about the peacemaking role of all the peacemakers in Bosnia-Herzegovina gave rise to concern, both in my case and in the case of all the other citizens of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and I really do not wish to comment on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Well, four days after the Serbian autonomous region of Eastern Herzegovina was formed, the Serbian autonomous region of Bosnia and Krajina was formed, too, so were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Did you see that as heralding the disintegration of the internal structure of Bosnia-Herzegovina along ethnic lines?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I saw the announcement, but not the disintegration. The disintegration is impossible.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: There was a huge amount of concern amongst the Croats and the Muslims at these apparently secessionist efforts on the part of the Serbs in September of 1991. I think that would be fair to say, and you would agree with that, would you not, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I will do that. But, Your Honours, can we please stick to the first defendant's case?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Well, let's just proceed along the path chronologically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If Counsel asks questions which are irrelevant, we'll stop him. But at the moment, he's not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Three days after the call to arms issued by President Stjepan Kljujic of the HDZ BiH, on September the 21st, 1991, that's when the convoy that Mr. Nice referred to in the direct examination was stopped at Kaonik; is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And that was a big JNA convoy carrying armed shipments to the Serbs in the JNA; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: You are wrong, or rather you were given the wrong information. It was not a big convoy, it was a small convoy which was intercepted by the paramilitary formation of the HDZ BH in the municipality of Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Large or small, though, it was headed for the JNA, wasn't it, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You were worried that those arms would actually be used to kill Muslims and to kill Croats, were you not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: To begin with, you need to know that nobody knew what was being transported. There was no counterintelligence service which would report what had been loaded onto those trucks. It could have been food or anything else. And, thirdly, we did not think it was a means -- an instrument of killing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Just a couple of days after September the 21st of 1991, something happened at the town of Ravno, and you mentioned it in your direct examination, and I wonder if you would be --

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: -- if you would be so good as to just tell the Judges what occurred at Ravno at the end of September 1991.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: If Your Honours permit me, may I complete the previous answer? Only one sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, and then deal with the question.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I should like to ask the Defence to be very precise. At Kaonik at that moment, JNA representatives, SDA representatives came, and Mr. Kordic went to negotiations together with them. He stepped aside, and he agreed that the next day they would all sit down in the hotel in Vitez and would continue the negotiations. He let the convoy through without any problem, but the moment he put his combatants -- rather his criminals -- to stop, they were ready to begin to kill people, and it was not the strategic material, which is what they noted among themselves. So the meeting was attended by Mr. Kordic, by Mr. Muhamed Cero, and the captain responsible for the convoy.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now could you answer the question, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Will you repeat it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Certainly. Could you tell the Judges of the Trial Chamber what happened at the town of Ravno towards the end of September 1991?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think you went slightly wrong there. Will you please think about the date again?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Well, you mentioned the town of Ravno, sir.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: It doesn't really matter. It doesn't really matter. I can answer, but you have to amend the documentation. The village of Ravno was razed to the ground by the Yugoslav People's Army. There was a cannon attack, and then an onslaught took place so that nobody stayed there. People that could move ran away. Those who stayed behind were killed, shovelled over with ground. This village of Ravno stopped existing, but it was not on the day that you mentioned. It happened much more -- a long time before that. In Bosnia-Herzegovina we believe that that was the beginning of the war. I don't know if I was too fast for interpreters. That is, we see that date as the beginning of the aggression against Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And the town of Ravno, the village of Ravno, was primarily a Croat community inside Bosnia-Herzegovina; isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: The village of Ravno is a Croat village in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and now it has been reconstructed, and it is a Croat village again, and it has even become a municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. But by September of 1991, all you're saying, sir, is that it was a smoking hole in the ground with no one left there, as a result of the attacks of the JNA inside Bosnia-Herzegovina. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. The HDZ BH, or more specifically Mr. Kljujic, protested vigorously with the presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the citizens of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and he insisted, indicating that this was the beginning of the aggression against Bosnia-Herzegovina by the JNA, but he was alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Do you recall a famous press conference or press announcement made by President Izetbegovic in connection with the attack on Ravno, sir, at which he announced to all of the citizens of Bosnia-Herzegovina that "This is not our war"?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember this nonsense.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: That particular announcement caused tremendous concern and worry and anxiety amongst the Croat community throughout Bosnia-Herzegovina, did it not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. It did not cause major fear among the Croats. It caused great fear among the citizens of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Muslims, Serbs and Croats. That is, citizens of Bosnia-Herzegovina began to fear.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: If I could turn to the next document chronologically, Your Honours, I believe it's Z18.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Mr. Sayers, before we proceed, before we move on to the next question, the witness told us that in relation to canonisation there were two positions, two views on that, and he explained them to us. We should like to know, what were the objectives expected of the canonisation?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: That's an excellent question, Judge Bennouna, and I'm sorry that I didn't cover it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Turning to the question posed to you by Judge Bennouna, Mr. Cicak, could you just explain for the Court what the objectives of this commission for canonisation were?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Bosnia-Herzegovina is divided into natural regions. Under the communist regime, they were regions Tuzla, Doboj, Zenica, Bihac, Mostar, and a number of others. It transpired, when Mr. Badinter came to Bosnia-Herzegovina, it proved proper to overcome the crisis by turning those natural regions into cantons. However, two views prevailed. Mr. Kljujic and others in the HDZ, that is, in the presidency of the HDZ, with other progressive forces, they said that every canton should be mixed, that is, that in each one of them, Muslims, Croats, and Serbs should live together. However, the Herzegovinian current, headed by Boban, Kordic and others, advocated a view -- and you can find it in a document, and I'm sorry that we glossed over that document too quickly and never drew attention to it -- it says that it has been the age-old aspiration to form those cantons and to annex them to the state of Croatia. In another document you can also find that the Croat part of the Security Council was to become part of the system of the organised defence of Croatia. So, you see, joining ethnically pure regions with the state of Croatia, both in terms of defence and in civil administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Did that respond to your question, Judge Bennouna?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Yes, thank you, but those people who discussed the canonisation, did they understand by it a federal structure, when they spoke about the canonisation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: They meant the structure of Bosnia-Herzegovina, absolutely federal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Sayers, it's now the time for the break.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank God.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I notice that so far you've covered five documents in an hour and a half. We really must make more progress after the adjournment. I don't want to put a limit on the length of cross-examination, but we must have regard to the time and the time this trial is taking. So I must ask you to speed up after the adjournment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I'll do my best to do that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You had, I understand, hoped or anticipated you would finish by the next adjournment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Actually, I gave that estimate to Mr. Nice at the end of the first day, and of course the witness covered a tremendous amount of territory which was not in any way heralded by the scanty summary of his purported testimony that we received, so to put it mildly, we had some scrambling to do over the weekend and last night, so I regret that it is taking a little longer than I anticipated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, perhaps you could put on as much speed as possible after the adjournment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Now the witness is responsible for this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: 20 minutes, I should have said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Sayers, one matter occurs to us, and it is this: You are going through it document by document. Is it possible to speed that process up without going through every single one?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour. I did not intend to do that, but I felt it was important to lay a proper historical foundation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Bearing in mind the injunction that we heard just before the break, Mr. Cicak, that brevity is to be commended, I have one final question for you on Exhibit Z16. I don't think you need to see the document, necessarily, but here's what it says. Paragraph 2: "The crisis staffs must be formed post-haste for three regional communities of the BH HDZ, namely: the Travnik regional community, the Herzegovina regional community, and the Posavina regional community." You don't disagree that that was a decision reached by the Security Council at the national level on September the 18th, 1991, do you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Esteemed colleague, I appreciate what you're saying and I understand what you're saying, but could I please have the Croatian interpretation of what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much indeed, sir. Now, if we could just turn our attention briefly to Exhibit Z18. I'm sorry. I don't think that there was a Croatian interpretation of that preceding question, so if I might just ask it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Can you understand me now, sir? How about now, Mr. Cicak?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Sorry about that.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: It's all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I just wanted to draw your attention to paragraph 2. I don't need to repeat it for the Trial Chamber, I'd just like you to agree that that reflects accurate a decision that was reached by the Security Council of the party at the national level on September the 18th, 1991.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: So there were three regional communities that were actually recognised by the party on the national level as of that time; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, the instructions -- oh, yes, yes, absolutely. I got a bit confused.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: No problem. Okay. Moving along to Exhibit Z18, I would just like to ask you a few questions in connection with that. If you take a look at paragraph 4, it is true, is it not, that the HDZ BiH advocated an independent and indivisible Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And you agreed with that, too; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: There wasn't any suggestion of secession of parts of Bosnia-Herzegovina to form an independent country with Croatia at this time, was there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: There was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Well, actually, the date of this document is October the 8th, 1991, and that's the very day that the declaration of Croatian independence became legally effective, is it not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, but this is Mr. Stjepan Kljujic's last document, or rather of the Crisis Staff that he had chaired, and this is the last text that he had written.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. And, indeed, if you take a look at paragraph 6, the Croatian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina were instructed not to contribute in any way to strains in relations with the Muslims; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Allow me to have a look.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Absolutely. Take your time.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your interpretation seems to be a bit different. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You agree that that's basically the sense of what the Croatian version of paragraph 6 says, what I've just said?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Absolutely. It is Mr. Stjepan Kljujic's recognisable style, or rather his way of thinking.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Nonetheless, though, the HDZ was continuing to develop its own policies and activities independently, and that's what the rest of that conclusion states; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Independently, but on the basis of the principle of an indivisible Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. If you just take a look at paragraph 9, there's a concern expressed there by the Security Council that crisis staffs have only been partially implemented and that the implementation of the conclusions regarding crisis staffs must be undertaken in all environments. You didn't disagree with this, did you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did, but that was impossible to implement. There were only three communities where it was possible to establish crisis staffs. That was Posavina, Herzegovina and Travnik, respectively.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Would you turn to paragraph 14, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Very gladly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: This is a decision made to establish a new newspaper called "The Herceg-Bosna", and there would be a three-person board basically responsible for its publication and preparation, including Mr. Kljujic; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes. There are three persons that are charged with this here; that is to say, Stjepan Kljujic, Miro Lasic and Ivan Markesic. However, as far as I know, this newspaper was never, ever published.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And according to paragraph 15, it was Mr. Kljujic, not Mr. Boban, who was responsible for coordinating work between the newly-independent country of Croatia and the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Let me have a look.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. According to paragraph 11, just to go back a little bit, do you recall any discussion at the local level of the importance of keeping proper records of personnel and equipment? Do you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know what equipment you have in mind. If you're talking about weapons, you have to rephrase your question. As for records, we talked about that concerning the young men who were supposed to go into the JNA. As regards these particular records that you mentioned, I don't know what you are referring to, so would you please be so kind as to rephrase your question or repeat it?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Well, if you don't know what the document is referring to, let's just move on, sir. Was there any concern expressed in the Croatian community, and in the Muslim community, actually, at this time, regarding a potentially significant problem with large numbers of refugees?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't think that it is a question of refugees.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: How about paragraph 18, then, of this document signed by Mr. Kljujic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: The municipal committees were directed to form commissions for the reception of refugees, were they not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And, indeed, there was a directive to cooperate with humanitarian organisations such as the Red Cross, Caritas and other humanitarian organisations, and you were aware of that directive, I take it, paragraph 19.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I am aware of that and we worked on this. But I think it is not a question of refugees who had come in, it is a question of preparing the organisation for receiving them. If there is a danger of war, then there might be refugees, and then the population should take them in. That is to say, every municipal board had to have certain services set up so they would carry out their duties when the time came. So it is not a question of refugees that were already coming in.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Stepping aside from this document a little, and before we go to the next one, isn't it true that at this time in the autumn of 1991, there was a significant degree of concern in the expatriate community of Croats living abroad outside of Bosnia-Herzegovina and that support, both financial and otherwise, was received from that expatriate community?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: There was not great concern, but there was great support, considerably so. The idea of Mr. Franjo Tudjman of a movement of all the Croats throughout the world, including the diaspora that fully responded to this call.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And people in countries like, for example, just to choose a few, Germany, Switzerland, Austria and the United States, actually sent in contributions to help Croats, didn't they? Right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, especially Australia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: If you would just take a look at Exhibit Z19, Z19, and I'm the first to say, Mr. Cicak, that this is somewhat illegible, but doesn't it appear to you to be a receipt for Deutschmarks, Swiss francs, Austrian shillings, U.S. dollars, and also the Swedish kronors?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know what you're asking me to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, the witness hasn't seen this document before, so there's very little point putting it to him. And no doubt we'll hear some evidence about it in due course.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I'll move on, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Just a couple of questions about the next exhibit, which is Exhibit Z20. This was a meeting of the regional community of the HDZ for the Travnik region held in Busovaca on November the 4th, 1991; is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Incidentally, Mr. Martin Udovicic was present for this meeting, was he not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I think he was together with Mr. Kordic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Would you take a look at the list of the attendees from the Travnik municipality? Mr. Zec, Mr. Gaso, Mr. Matisic and Mr. Udovicic attended, did they not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And so did you, sir, did you not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it says so here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Sure. You agree with the conclusion that is contained on paragraph 3 of the conclusions, that the HDZ municipal boards were to maintain the closest cooperation possible with the SDA, the Party of Democratic Action boards, in order to avoid all conflicts and disagreements; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
utterances.text: (Inaudible response)

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: That subject was discussed in this meeting, was it not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN CICAK (Resumed)
